section_summary: This section follows Japanese fishing and research vessels operating near Alaska in 1935, including proposed visits to Aleutian and Pribilof ports. It contains two drafts of a bill regulating foreign fishing vessels, reports on the Ryokai Maru and Taihoku Maru, and correspondence over courtesies for the Hakuyo Maru and Hakuho Maru. Later papers examine the legal status of a 1911 fur-seal conference protocol and investigate the Hakuho Maru’s approach to Amchitka.

subfiles.title: Fishing operations of the Ryokai Maru and Taihoku Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s notice that two vessels and their auxiliaries sailed from Hakodate for Bering Sea fishing grounds.
subfiles.summary: Hull reports the vessels’ planned crab fishery and fish-meal operations and promises Commerce the Embassy’s fuller report.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file note
subfiles.about: A fragmentary handwritten note concerning a radio report is largely illegible.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary handwritten note; its subject cannot be established reliably from the OCR.

subfiles.title: Conversation on draft fishing-vessel bill
subfiles.doc_type: memorandum of conversation with duplicate copies
subfiles.about: Records State’s informal approval of an interdepartmental bill to regulate Japanese fishing vessels in American waters.
subfiles.summary: Major Chipman sought State’s review before submitting the draft to the President. Dooman found its purpose satisfactory but noted State was not on the committee; Chipman would disclose that State had been consulted informally. The memorandum appears in repeated copies.

subfiles.title: First draft bill regulating foreign fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Sets documentary requirements, boarding powers, penalties, and entry rules for foreign-owned vessels and fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: The draft requires foreign-owned vessels in U.S. territorial waters to carry registration, crew and passenger lists, and cargo manifests. It authorizes boarding, fines, arrests, and forfeiture for specified violations, regulates port entry and clearance, preserves treaty obligations, and gives Commerce enforcement powers.

subfiles.title: Revised bill regulating vessels in the fisheries
subfiles.about: Revises proposed federal controls over foreign-owned vessels and participation in U.S. fisheries.
subfiles.summary: This clean draft specifies ship papers and manifests, boarding authority, penalties, and forfeiture for non-U.S. vessels fishing in U.S. waters. It exempts small vessels from one documentary provision, sets entry and clearance rules, protects existing treaties, and delays effectiveness for six months.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note on Hakuyo Maru itinerary
subfiles.about: Gives proposed June and July calls and requests ordinary facilities for the Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The Ambassador says the training ship cannot change its schedule, will avoid U.S. territorial waters at Bristol Bay, and considers an American naval escort unnecessary for calls at Dutch Harbor and St. Paul Island.

subfiles.title: State reply concerning Hakuyo Maru visits
subfiles.about: Confirms that the Hakuyo Maru may receive courtesies at Dutch Harbor and St. Paul Island under proposed arrangements.
subfiles.summary: State confirms an oral assurance despite possible U.S. naval activity and asks Japan to follow the arrangements offered on May 2.

subfiles.title: Phillips conversation with Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: Clarifies why State still sought naval arrangements for the Hakuyo Maru’s Alaskan visit.
subfiles.summary: Phillips explained that American vessels would remain in Alaskan waters after maneuvers ended, so the proposed courtesies should stand. The Ambassador agreed to inform Tokyo and requested a confirming note.

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment of canceled Hakuyo Maru calls
subfiles.about: Acknowledges notice that the Hakuyo Maru would skip Dutch Harbor and St. Paul Island.
subfiles.summary: Navy notes the ship will practice in open Bristol Bay waters, then proceed to Russian waters.

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment of Bering Sea fishing report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges State’s report of scheduled Japanese fishing operations in the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Navy thanks State for information about Japanese ships headed to Bering Sea fishing grounds.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on Ryokai Maru and Taihoku Maru
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Embassy Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese Foreign Office letter about fishing vessels bound for the Bering Sea.
subfiles.summary: Neville encloses Togo’s vessel details and reiterates the Embassy’s understanding that the ships will not fish for salmon.

subfiles.title: Togo letter listing Bering Sea fishing vessels
subfiles.about: Lists two Japanese fishing ships and fourteen auxiliary vessels departing Hakodate.
subfiles.summary: Togo describes crab fishing and fish-meal work and says the vessels are expected to remain on the high seas.

subfiles.title: State transmittal of fishing-vessel despatch to Commerce
subfiles.about: Sends Commerce the Embassy despatch and Togo’s vessel report.
subfiles.summary: Forwards additional information on the Ryokai Maru and Taihoku Maru’s Bering Sea operations.

subfiles.title: State transmittal of fishing-vessel despatch to Navy
subfiles.about: Sends Navy the Embassy despatch and Togo’s vessel report.
subfiles.summary: Forwards additional information on the Ryokai Maru and Taihoku Maru’s Bering Sea operations.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note on Hakuho Maru cruise
subfiles.about: Announces the Hakuho Maru’s fur-seal investigation cruise and requests courtesies at listed Alaskan ports.
subfiles.summary: The note invokes the 1911 fur-seal conference protocol, names expert Katsumi Miyataka, and gives scheduled calls at Attu, Atka, St. Paul, St. George, and Dutch Harbor, with possible refuge elsewhere in storms.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment of Hakuho Maru request
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japan’s proposed Hakuho Maru cruise and request for port courtesies.
subfiles.summary: Hull records the proposed fur-seal mission and says State is consulting other federal departments before replying.

subfiles.title: State inquiry to Navy on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Asks whether Navy objects to the Hakuho Maru’s proposed Aleutian and Pribilof visits.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the Japanese note, recalls similar cruises in 1933 and 1934, and requests customary facilities if Navy has no objection.

subfiles.title: State inquiry to Commerce on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Asks whether Commerce objects to the Hakuho Maru’s proposed cruise.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the Japanese request and asks Commerce to arrange customary courtesies if it has no objection.

subfiles.title: State notice to Labor on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Requests customary facilities for the Hakuho Maru and its crew.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Japan’s proposed fur-seal cruise and asks Labor to extend usual courtesies if unobjectionable.

subfiles.title: State notice to Interior on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Requests customary facilities for the Hakuho Maru’s proposed Alaskan calls.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Japan’s proposed fur-seal cruise and asks Interior to extend usual courtesies if unobjectionable.

subfiles.title: State notice to Agriculture on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Requests customary facilities for the Hakuho Maru’s proposed Alaskan calls.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Japan’s proposed fur-seal cruise and asks Agriculture to extend usual courtesies if unobjectionable.

subfiles.title: State notice to Treasury on Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Requests customary facilities for the Hakuho Maru’s proposed Alaskan calls.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Japan’s proposed fur-seal cruise and asks Treasury to extend usual courtesies if unobjectionable.

subfiles.title: Phillips memorandum on Navy response
subfiles.about: Records a conversation urging Navy to handle the Hakuho Maru request as it had in 1934.
subfiles.summary: Phillips told Captain Townsend that objecting to a cruise invoking the fur-seal protocol would be embarrassing.

subfiles.title: Navy response on Hakuho Maru visits
subfiles.about: Declines to object to the Hakuho Maru’s visits but proposes a U.S. escort ship and Japanese-speaking officer.
subfiles.summary: Navy voices concern about foreign vessels gathering military information and proposes an escort to provide courtesies during the visit.

subfiles.title: State objection to escorting Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Urges Navy to treat the Hakuho Maru’s visits as routine without a ship or officer escort.
subfiles.summary: State argues that an escort might conflict with the purpose of the fur-seal conference protocol and differ from the previous year’s treatment. Hull also confidentially notes planned talks with Japan to protect Bristol Bay salmon and asks Navy to avoid action that could hinder a treaty.

subfiles.title: Treasury arrangements for Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Authorizes the Juneau customs collector to extend customary courtesies to the Hakuho Maru.
subfiles.summary: Treasury directs its Juneau collector to assist the ship during its June and July Alaskan visits.

subfiles.title: Navy agrees to routine treatment of Hakuho Maru
subfiles.about: Confirms naval commanders will treat the Hakuho Maru’s visits as routine.
subfiles.summary: Navy withdraws its proposal to offer an escort ship and officer representative.

subfiles.title: Protocol Division routing note
subfiles.about: Advises routine handling of the Hakuho Maru case following State’s letter to Navy.
subfiles.summary: Dooman advises that Protocol may handle the vessel’s visit as routine.

subfiles.title: State approval of Hakuho Maru itinerary
subfiles.about: Approves the Hakuho Maru’s scheduled calls and promises ordinary facilities.
subfiles.summary: State informs Japan that the fur-seal cruise is approved and arrangements have been made for customary courtesies at the listed ports.

subfiles.title: Note on Japan’s fur-seal share
subfiles.about: Records a decision to defer inquiry about whether Japan would take fur-seal skins rather than sale proceeds.
subfiles.summary: Bowers agrees to take no action while Alaskan fishery negotiations are contemplated.

subfiles.title: Commerce response on Hakuho Maru and fur-seal skins
subfiles.about: Accepts the Hakuho Maru’s visit while asking about Japan’s planned fur-seal payment share.
subfiles.summary: Commerce sees no objection and will extend courtesies. It disputes the suggestion of poaching and asks whether Japan wants physical delivery of its treaty share of fur-seal skins.

subfiles.title: Labor arrangements for Hakuho Maru personnel
subfiles.about: Notifies immigration officials to extend lawful courtesies if the Hakuho Maru seeks refuge.
subfiles.summary: The Seattle district director will assist the vessel’s personnel if it enters an Alaskan port in bad weather.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of Japanese fishing report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the report on Japanese vessels fishing near the Alaska Peninsula.
subfiles.summary: Commerce notes assurances about high-seas operations and no salmon fishing, while stressing concern for American fishery interests.

subfiles.title: Navy acknowledgment of Togo’s vessel report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Embassy despatch and Togo’s letter on Japanese Bering Sea vessels.
subfiles.summary: Navy thanks State for forwarding the fishing-vessel information.

subfiles.title: Naval intelligence report on Japanese fishery activity
subfiles.about: Relays Coast Guard observations of Japanese vessels near the Pribilofs.
subfiles.summary: An officer reports a large floating cannery, nearby tenders, radio traffic, and the Ryokai Maru’s initially unanswered radio call.

subfiles.title: Navy inquiry about an apparent itinerary change
subfiles.about: Requests an explanation for the Hakuho Maru’s reported appearance near Amchitka.
subfiles.summary: Navy encloses a survey expedition report and considers renewing plans for an escort.

subfiles.title: Aleutian survey telegram on vessel near Amchitka
subfiles.about: Reports a vessel believed to be Japanese approaching Constantine Harbor on June 24.
subfiles.summary: A survey boat sighted the vessel close to Amchitka; the report speculates about interest in sea otters.

subfiles.title: Navy transmittal of vessel photographs
subfiles.about: Forwards photographs labeled Hakuho Maru and Hakuyo Maru.
subfiles.summary: The cover letter offers the two ship photographs for State’s files on Aleutian visits.

subfiles.title: Treaty Division memorandum on Fur Seal Conference Protocol X
subfiles.about: Explains the status of the 1911 conference protocol invoked for Japanese scientific visits.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum distinguishes conference minutes from binding treaty provisions and reproduces Protocol X, which accepted scientific visits in principle at mutually convenient times. It concludes that the proposal was omitted from the convention and creates no definite legal obligation, though refusal would need explanation.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs request for protocol interpretation
subfiles.about: Asks Treaty Division to identify the protocol cited by the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs cannot locate a relevant protocol in its treaty reference.

subfiles.title: Navy request for Protocol X text
subfiles.about: Requests a copy of the fur-seal conference protocol cited for the Hakuho Maru visit.
subfiles.summary: Navy says its files contain no record of the cited protocol.

subfiles.title: State reply to Navy quoting Protocol X
subfiles.about: Supplies Navy with the text of Protocol X of the 1911 fur-seal conference.
subfiles.summary: State explains that the protocols are conference minutes and quotes the passage accepting scientific visits in principle at mutually convenient times.

subfiles.title: State letter to Commerce quoting Protocol X
subfiles.about: Provides Commerce the text of the protocol cited by Japan.
subfiles.summary: State reproduces its explanation to Navy that Protocol X is a conference minute concerning scientific visits to fur-seal breeding grounds.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser memorandum on Protocol X
subfiles.about: Recommends sending Navy the protocol text without a formal opinion on its legal force.
subfiles.summary: The adviser agrees Protocol X creates no definite treaty obligation because its terms were omitted from the convention. He nonetheless sees grounds for cooperation under the convention and advises against needlessly raising a legal dispute.

subfiles.title: Turner inquiry to Kuroda
subfiles.about: Asks Japan to investigate reports that the Hakuho Maru entered unlisted U.S. territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: Kuroda agrees to check the vessel’s movements and report back.

subfiles.title: Kuroda explanation of Hakuho Maru approach
subfiles.about: Records Japan’s explanation of the Hakuho Maru’s June 24 approach near Amchitka.
subfiles.summary: Kuroda says fog led the ship to approach land to confirm its position, after which it turned north without entering port or anchoring. He cites the Embassy’s earlier notice that necessity might require entry at other points.

subfiles.title: State explanation to Navy of Hakuho Maru sighting
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s explanation for the Hakuho Maru’s appearance near Constantine Harbor.
subfiles.summary: State relays that the vessel approached land in fog to fix its position, then continued north without anchoring or entering a port. Japan also cites its earlier reservation for necessary refuge.

subfiles.title: Bering Sea Patrol report on Japanese visitor
subfiles.from: H. R. Searles, Commander, Bering Sea Patrol Force
subfiles.about: Reports questioning Shigeru Fugii about his visit to Unalaska and recommends further investigation.
subfiles.summary: Searles recounts Fugii’s claim that he was searching for lost aviator Kiyoshi Homma, but finds his conduct suspicious. The report continues beyond this section.
